title: Insight Into the Blood‐Feeding Patterns of Culex Mosquitoes: A Global Comprehensive Meta‐Analysis Across Spatial and Seasonal Dimensions
content:
ABSTRACT

Aim

Culex mosquitoes are key vectors of several arboviruses and other pathogens, and their blood-feeding patterns vary with environmental factors. This study aims to assess how biogeographic realm, habitat type, and seasonality influence host-use patterns in medically relevant Culex species using a global meta-analysis.

Location

Global.

Time Period

1967–2025.

Major Taxa Considered

Culex mosquito species of medical importance: Cx. pipiens s.l., Cx. quinquefasciatus, Cx. tarsalis, Cx. erraticus, Cx. restuans, and Cx. nigripalpus.

Methods

A meta-analysis was conducted using 149 published articles comprising 31,270 observations on blood-feeding patterns of six Culex species. The effects of biogeographic realm, habitat type, and seasonality on host choice were statistically assessed and compared across species.

Results

Species varied in their degree of host specificity, showing a predominant tendency toward ornithophagy. Blood-feeding behaviour varied across biogeographic realms, Cx. pipiens s.l. maintained high feeding on wild birds in the Nearctic and Palearctic, but showed increased contributions from humans and domestic birds in the Neotropical realm and higher feeding on mammals in the Afrotropical region, while Cx. quinquefasciatus displayed a more plastic pattern, with different host groups predominating depending on the region (e.g., wild birds in the Nearctic, domestic birds in the Palearctic, and humans in the Afrotropical realm). Habitat type also influenced feeding patterns, with urbanized habitats associated with increased feeding on humans and domesticated animals (e.g., domestic birds and farm mammals), compared to non-urban settings. Seasonal effects varied among species: Cx. quinquefasciatus showed increased mammalian feeding during autumn, while Cx. pipiens s.l. exhibited a marked shift toward mammalian feeding in autumn despite predominantly avian feeding during spring and summer.

Main Conclusions

Blood-feeding patterns in Culex mosquitoes are strongly influenced by environmental context, including geography, habitat, and seasonality. Integrating these environmental drivers in assessing the mosquito-host interaction is essential to improve the predictions on mosquito abundance and manage mosquito-borne disease transmission.
